sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
It's 7.30 in the morning on Saturday in Kiev.
sentences.zh: 基辅时间周六早上 7 点 30 分。

sentences.en: Last night, President Zelensky was standing outside the government building and trying to reassure his people.
sentences.zh: 昨晚，泽连斯基总统站在政府大楼外，试图安抚他的民众。

sentences.en: He was standing with other government officials.
sentences.zh: 他和其他政府官员站在一起。

sentences.en: The head of the fraction is here.
The head of the presidential office is here.
sentences.zh: 总统办公室主任在这儿。

sentences.en: And points to each of the men standing behind him.
sentences.zh: 他指了指站在他身后的每个人。

sentences.en: And he's telling people we're here.
sentences.zh: 他在告诉大家，我们都在这儿。

sentences.en: We're going to defend our country.
sentences.zh: 我们要保卫我们的国家。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the battle between Russian and Ukrainian forces came to Ukraine's capital of Kiev,
sentences.zh: 周末期间，俄罗斯与乌克兰军队之间的战斗蔓延到了乌克兰首都基辅，

sentences.en: transforming a once vibrant, bustling city into a war zone.
sentences.zh: 将一个曾经充满活力、熙熙攘攘的城市变成了一个战区。

sentences.en: And the question was, would the Russian military quickly overrun the city?
sentences.zh: 问题是，俄军会迅速占领这座城市吗？

sentences.en: Or would Ukrainians, despite being outgunned, somehow find a way to defend it?
sentences.zh: 还是说，尽管武器处于劣势，乌克兰人仍会想方设法保卫它？

sentences.en: Once again, Sabrina Tavernisi reports from Kiev.
sentences.zh: 再次由萨布丽娜·塔维尔尼西从基辅发回报道。
今天是 2 月 28 日，星期一。

sentences.en: I'm walking out to the main street in front of the hotel.
sentences.zh: 我正走向酒店正门前的干道。

sentences.en: I just saw an ambulance go by.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚看到一辆救护车驶过。

sentences.en: A fair number of cars on the street this morning.
sentences.zh: 今天早上街上的车还挺多的。

sentences.en: We're on our way to a blood bank and a recruiting center where people are getting guns and volunteering in civilian defense forces.
sentences.zh: 我们正前往一个血库和一个招募中心，那里的人们正在领取枪支并自愿加入民间防卫力量。

sentences.en: It was a really loud night.
There was fighting as close as the zoo, which is kind of in the western part of the city.
sentences.zh: 战斗声最近的到了动物园，那差不多在城市的西部。

sentences.en: So Russian forces reached quite far, in fact, into Kiev last night.
sentences.zh: 所以昨晚俄军实际上深入到了基辅相当远的地方。

sentences.en: And it was there was also small arms fire, which might have been a kind of a saboteur group of Russian soldiers or fighters not far from the hotel.
sentences.zh: 而且还有轻武器射击的声音，可能是一小群俄罗斯士兵或武装人员的破坏小组，离酒店不远。

sentences.en: I heard that one as well several times during the night.
sentences.zh: 昨晚我也好几次听到那个声音。

sentences.en: And yeah, we're going to go out and and check things out this morning.
sentences.zh: 是的，今天早上我们要出去查看一下情况。

sentences.en: OK, so I'm standing outside an office where people are signing up to do territorial defense work or receive weapons.
sentences.zh: 好的，我现在站在一个办公室外面，人们在那里登记进行国土防卫工作或领取武器。

sentences.en: People, the line is quite long.
A lot of men milling around, holding rifles on their backs, guarding the gate.
sentences.zh: 许多男人在周围转悠，背着步枪，守卫着大门。

sentences.en: The man says, where do we where do we sign up?
sentences.zh: 那个人说，我们在哪里登记？

sentences.en: And this gentleman is sending him to a different building.
sentences.zh: 然后这位先生把他指引到另一栋楼。

sentences.en: OK, I'm going to go try to talk to some people who have come to sign up.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要去试着跟一些前来登记的人聊聊。

sentences.en: I'm a journalist from The New York Times.
What is, what are you, why are you here today?
sentences.zh: 你今天来这里是为了什么？

sentences.en: I'm living here, just in that area.
sentences.zh: 我就住在这儿，就在那个区域。

sentences.en: This is where you live, this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这是你住的地方，这个社区。

sentences.en: What's it called, Andrei, this neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 这个社区叫什么名字，安德烈？

sentences.en: And I feel I need to protect my house, my home place.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我需要保护我的房子，我的家园。

sentences.en: They think they get us free, but it's lie.
sentences.zh: 他们以为他们能解放我们，但这是谎言。

sentences.en: It's completely lie, because they want to destroy us.
sentences.zh: 完全是谎言，因为他们想要摧毁我们。

sentences.en: They are quite stupid, because for all of that time, for 30 years, they didn't identify us as a nation, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 他们挺愚蠢的，因为在过去的整整 30 年里，他们没有把我们认同一个民族，但事实确实如此。

sentences.en: They always said, oh, Ukraine's not a nation, but Ukraine is a nation.
sentences.zh: 他们总是说，哦，乌克兰不是一个民族，但乌克兰是一个民族。

sentences.en: So they need to kill a lot of people to kill nation, and it's not possible.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要杀死很多人才能消灭这个民族，而这是不可能的。

sentences.en: So we're walking along the site of this really major firefight.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正沿着这场特大枪战的现场步行。

sentences.en: There's a Ukrainian position dug in over the railroad tracks, and there's debris all over the street, pieces of branches, pieces of concrete.
sentences.zh: 铁轨上方挖有一个乌克兰阵地，街上到处都是残骸，有树枝碎片、混凝土碎片。
看起来像是各种玻璃弹片。

sentences.en: So a major, major firefight here.
sentences.zh: 这里发生了一场极其激烈的枪战。

sentences.en: Two trucks look like two transport trucks.
sentences.zh: 两辆卡车看起来像两辆运输卡车。

sentences.en: Very, very strong smell of burned, maybe tires, rubber.
sentences.zh: 有一股非常非常强烈的烧焦气味，可能是轮胎或橡胶味。

sentences.en: Two completely burned out and just smoldering transport trucks.
sentences.zh: 两辆运输卡车完全烧毁了，还在冒着烟。

sentences.en: There's a kind of a slick, oily stain around one of them.
sentences.zh: 其中一辆周围有一层滑腻的油渍。

sentences.en: Right now, they're Ukrainian soldiers picking through the wreckage of the two trucks.
sentences.zh: 现在，有乌克兰士兵正在这两辆卡车的残骸中翻找。

sentences.en: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven Ukrainian soldiers.
sentences.zh: 一个、两个、三个、四个、五个、六个、七个乌克兰士兵。

sentences.en: They're putting what looks like munitions in small wooden boxes that they have salvaged from this firefight.
sentences.zh: 他们把看起来像军火的东西放进他们从这场枪战中抢救出来的小木箱里。

sentences.en: This is the sound of a Ukrainian soldier digging positions above the highway.
sentences.zh: 这是乌克兰士兵在公路上方挖掘阵地的声音。

sentences.en: Are you, you're digging a position here?

sentences.zh: 亚历山大，很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: And you know this problem in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 你知道乌克兰的这个局势。

sentences.en: And we understand that war is inescapable now, so we're digging in positions.
sentences.zh: 我们明白战争现在是不可避免的，所以我们正在构筑阵地。

sentences.en: The war, it's not that it's inescapable, it's already started.
sentences.zh: 战争倒不是说不可避免，它已经开始了。

sentences.en: We have to protect all of the peaceful people who stayed here and who are trying to leave
sentences.zh: 我们必须保护所有留在这里的平和百姓，以及那些正试图离开

sentences.en: Kiev so that they can peacefully leave.
sentences.zh: 基辅以便能安全离开的人。

sentences.en: Sasha has some blood on his cheek.
sentences.zh: 萨莎的脸颊上有一些血迹。

sentences.en: He said it's just a scratch.
I think we should try to talk to them.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该试着跟他们谈谈。

sentences.en: God, that is, that is really quite terrifying sight, these trucks.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这些卡车，真的是相当骇人的景象。

sentences.en: We're going back to our cocktail.
sentences.zh: 我们要回我们的鸡尾酒那儿去了。
这里的人非常非常紧张。

sentences.en: Oh, a bunch of Molotov cocktails.
sentences.zh: 哦，一堆莫洛托夫鸡尾酒（燃烧瓶）。

sentences.en: Watch out, they're going to freak out if you take a picture.
sentences.zh: 小心，如果你拍照他们会抓狂的。

sentences.en: A bunch of Molotov cocktails here at the base of a tree.
sentences.zh: 树根这里有一堆莫洛托夫鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: A box of, looks like they're in, actually in beer bottles.
sentences.zh: 一箱，看起来它们其实是用啤酒瓶装的。

sentences.en: God, I still can't believe this is happening in Kiev.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我还是不敢相信这正在基辅发生。

sentences.en: So we're going down into the parking garage of this building where the firefight was outside of to look, to talk to people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要走到外面发生过交火的那栋建筑的地下停车场去看看，跟人们聊聊。

sentences.en: There's a trail of blood going into the parking garage.
sentences.zh: 通往地下停车场有一道血迹。

sentences.en: The gentleman who's leading us says it's a shelter.
sentences.zh: 带路的这位先生说那是一个避难所。

sentences.en: So we're going down into kind of a cavernous area, clearly, parking garage.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正走在一个像洞穴一样宽阔的区域，很明显，是停车场。

sentences.en: There are men and women walking up on the other side of us.
sentences.zh: 我们身侧有男男女女正走上来。

sentences.en: Um, I'm walking along and seeing, seeing blood.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一边走一边看，看到了血迹。

sentences.en: I see blood on a footprint.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个脚印上有血。

sentences.en: So somebody's, somebody's footprint with blood and it's leading to a boot that is lying by itself.
sentences.zh: 所以那是某人的、某人的带血脚印，它通向一只孤零零躺着靴子。

sentences.en: It's clearly wet, but I'm looking at the boot and it seems to have a look.
sentences.zh: 它明显是湿的，但我看着这只靴子，它似乎有一种样子。

sentences.en: Look at the plastic, uh, the plastic thing has blood on it as well.
sentences.zh: 看那个塑料，呃，那个塑料袋上也有血。

sentences.en: A young man was saying that, uh, the, it happened around four or five in the morning and he helped bring the wounded, uh, down into the parking garage that's now a bomb shelter.
sentences.zh: 一个年轻人说，呃，这发生在凌晨四五点左右，他帮忙把伤员，呃，抬到了现在作为防空洞的地下停车场。

sentences.en: He's pointing out, look, there, there's the blood.
sentences.zh: 他指着说，看，那里，那里有血。

sentences.en: Oh, he didn't, he didn't die.
That's the trail of the blood.
We dragged him and we carried him with our hands.
sentences.zh: 我们把他拖过来，用手抬过来的。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着你300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个像美丽的50年历史艺术品般的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: We're going upstairs to the blood donation.
This appears to be some sort of a hospital or health center or something.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是某种医院、健康中心之类的机构。

sentences.en: And people are lined up along the stairs.
sentences.zh: 人们在楼梯旁排起了长队。

sentences.en: So I'm a reporter from The New York Times.
Why did you guys come today?

sentences.zh: 是什么把你们吸引到这里来的？

sentences.en: I think it's just a little thing which we can do right now to support our guys who are fighting for our independence.
sentences.zh: 我想这只是我们现在能为支持那些为我们独立而战的战士们做的一点小事。
我在自己的土地上过得很好。
我在自己的国家过得很好。

sentences.en: And it's just a little thing what I can do.
sentences.zh: 这只是我能做的一点小事。

sentences.en: And now I can take just a little of my blood to support the bodies of my people.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以抽出我的一点点血来支持我同胞的身体。

sentences.en: How was last night for you?
Just a little bit because it was bombing and it was sirens.
sentences.zh: 只睡了一点点，因为有轰炸还有警报。

sentences.en: We were scared just on the first day.
sentences.zh: 我们只在第一天感到害怕。

sentences.en: Irina, how are you yourself feeling right now?
sentences.zh: 伊莉娜，你现在自己感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: And I want to live my peaceful life.
sentences.zh: 而我想过我平静的生活。

sentences.en: I don't want to have war on my land.
sentences.zh: 我不想在我的土地上有战争。
这就是为什么我很愤怒。
现在是星期六下午3点42分。

sentences.en: I have lots of boarded up windows
sentences.zh: 我看到很多用木板封上的窗户

sentences.en: and tape and plastic on windows to prevent them from shattering.
sentences.zh: 还有贴在窗户上的胶带和塑料布，用来防止它们碎裂。

sentences.en: Really, really has the look of
a city that has closed down and expects a storm.
sentences.zh: 城市已经关闭并等待风暴来临的感觉。

sentences.en: I'm on my way to go inside the metro where people are taking shelter overnight.
sentences.zh: 我正前往地铁内部，人们在那里过夜避难。

sentences.en: There's now a checkpoint to get into the metro and the guy who's guarding it is asking me for my passport so I have to show it to him.
sentences.zh: 现在进地铁有一个检查站，守卫的家伙在向我要护照，所以我得给他看。

sentences.en: I thought it was just a question.
She said the metro isn't working but you're welcome to go down.
sentences.zh: 她说地铁不运行，不过欢迎你下去。

sentences.en: So it's getting close to curfew.
These Soviet metros are deep, built deep, deep into the ground
sentences.zh: 这些苏联时期的地铁很深，深深地修建在地下

sentences.en: because they were originally designed as bomb shelters by the Soviets
sentences.zh: 因为它们最初是由苏联人设计作为防空洞的

sentences.en: in the event of a nuclear attack.
This one is very deep off the street.
and white marble walls and there's a giant kind of semicircle, very thick metal-plated opening that is the entrance to it but that can be closed up in the event of a bomb attack,
sentences.zh: 还有白色大理石墙壁，这里有一个巨大的半圆形、非常厚的金属镀层开口，这是它的入口，但在炸弹袭击时可以关闭，

sentences.en: kind of like being sealed up in a safe.
sentences.zh: 有点像被密封在保险箱里。
并盯着这条自动扶梯往下看时，

sentences.en: it's really almost as far as the eye can see.
sentences.zh: 真的是几乎一眼望不到头。

sentences.en: It is hard to overstate just how deep into the earth this escalator goes.
sentences.zh: 很难夸大这条自动扶梯深入地下到底有多深。

sentences.en: yeah, I'm just going to walk down.
It's going to take me a while.
Okay, we're getting close to the bottom.
is just sitting on the tracks in front of them with its doors open.
sentences.zh: 就停在他们面前的铁轨上，车门开着。

sentences.en: a few wheelie bags in this one.
sentences.zh: 这里有几个带轮子的包。

sentences.en: So Yulia and Andrey and two very, very cute little kids.
sentences.zh: 所以尤莉娅和安德烈，还有两个非常非常可爱的孩子。

sentences.en: And Gleb is a year and a half.

sentences.zh: 你们在这里过得怎么样？

sentences.en: We were here for a second night.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里待了第二个晚上。

sentences.en: I'm hoping that it will be safer than home.
sentences.zh: 我希望这里能比家里安全。

sentences.en: I can't imagine that this is happening.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: He's saying, I can't understand that this is happening.
sentences.zh: 他说，我无法理解这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: I want a metaphor for people to understand how much it is.
sentences.zh: 我想找个比喻，让大家明白这有多严重。

sentences.en: It's just like a complete nightmare.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场彻头彻尾的噩梦。
所以我现在正在和莉娜交谈。

sentences.en: My grandmother told me how terrible it was when there was bombing and she had two little children, about these age children.
sentences.zh: 我祖母曾跟我讲过，当年轰炸时有多可怕，她当时有两个小孩子，差不多就像这些孩子这么大。

sentences.en: She grasped the two children to her chest
sentences.zh: 她把两个孩子紧紧抱在胸前

sentences.en: and the Germans were shooting down.
This is like my grandmother running from the Germans shooting.
sentences.zh: 这就像我的祖母躲避着德国人的枪击逃跑一样。

sentences.en: I myself am a grandmother and these are my grandchildren and I am in the same situation.
sentences.zh: 我自己也是个祖母，这些是我的孙子孙女，而我也身处同样的境地。

sentences.en: My mother died and they didn't see this.
sentences.zh: 我母亲去世了，他们没有看到这一幕。
